Adversary

/AD-ver-sair-ee/ - the stress falls on AD · noun

Hear It

What It Means

Adversary means an opponent or enemy in a contest or conflict.

The crossword setter thinks of Monday's solver as a gentle adversary, to be beaten fairly or not at all.

Worked Example

The heist series runs on its two poles: Inspector Malle, who has chased the thief Aristide across nine books, and Aristide, who mails the inspector a taunting postcard from every city he slips out of. Each exists to defeat the other; neither, the author admits, would be worth a page alone. They are adversaries in the oldest storybook sense.

Adversary is the exact word because it names an opponent or enemy in a contest or conflict — someone set against you, whose aims cross yours. It says nothing about hatred: the inspector rather admires the thief. What makes them adversaries is the standing conflict between them, not any heat behind it.

How Adversary Sits Among Its Neighbors

Synonyms — open each to see how it differs

foe

foe: the plain, storybook word for the same role

enemy

enemy: carries real hatred; an adversary may respect you and still work to beat you

Antonyms

ally

ally: someone on your side of the conflict

supporter

supporter: someone actively backing your cause

How Strong Is It? — contender → adversary → archenemy

contender vs. adversary

contender vs. adversary: A contender is simply in the field, chasing the same prize as everyone else; an adversary is set against you in particular.

archenemy vs. adversary

archenemy vs. adversary: Archenemy goes past adversary — the one defining enemy of a lifetime, the name that darkens the whole story.

Build the Word

The pieces

Prefix — ad-

Prefix — ad-: toward, against

Root — vers

Root — vers: to turn

Suffix — -ary

Suffix — -ary: one who

Put it together

Put it together: Ad- (toward, against) + vers (to turn) + -ary (one who) = one turned against you. Latin adversarius was literally the person facing you from the other side — in court, in war, across the board. English kept the posture: an adversary is whoever stands turned your way, intent on stopping you.

Use the root in a new word: anniversary

Use the root in a new word: anniversary: An anniversary is the day the year has turned all the way around to the same date again.

Root Check

Word Choice

neutral / formal

Adversary names whoever stands against you in a real conflict — courtroom, battlefield, championship bracket. Keep it apart from this unit's rival, which needs no ill will at all: rivals chase the same prize, while an adversary is set against you in particular. When the relationship itself is built from opposition, the adjective is this unit's adversarial.
